newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end higher on fund buying, politics.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end higher on fund buying, politics.

text.p: Thai stocks advanced for the fourth consecutive trading day on Monday in anticipation of some political changes after this week's no-confidence debate and on continued buying by a private fund, brokers said.

The SET index, which hit its intraday peak at 1,061.43, or up 21.78, shortly after the lunch break, ended up 19.22 points to 1,058.87. Total turnover was 5.3 billion baht. The SET-50 index gained 1.62 points to 81.24.
"Investors bought shares today on high expectations that there would be some political changes after the no-confidence debate against the prime minister," said one broker.
Opposition parties are expected to grill Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa during the no-confidence debate in parliament which will start on Wednesday.
"The private fund was also seen actively buying stocks which focused heavily on finance, bank and communication counters today," said Chetta Meemangkang of Prime Finance and Securities.
Part of the 15.7 billion baht fund, contributed by commercial banks and brokerages, has been investing in the battered market since September 6.
Brokers said gains on Wall Street on Friday and some regional markets earlier today also helped boost sentiment on the Thai market, which had tumbled earlier this month.
Finance One topped the active list, gaining two baht to 103. Bangkok Bank rose two to 220 while Shinawatra Computer and Communications gained 14 to 408 and Electricity Generating surged one to 71.50.
Chetta said the SET index is expected to move sideways on Tuesday as it has risen for four days straight.
Support is seen around 1,040 points and resistance around 1,080 on Tuesday, brokers said. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
